title: SSH hardening lab: tighten a server, watch it defend itself
summary: An SSH server to harden and a client to probe it from, on an isolated segment (172.20.2.0/24). The exercises tighten sshd_config, let fail2ban ban the client after a few wrong logins and then clear it, hide SSH behind a port-knock sequence, and look at the server the way a scan would. fail2ban ignores the host-facing NAT network, so nothing here ever cuts off vmctl's own SSH. Ported from qlab's ssh-lab.

exercises.title: SSH anatomy
exercises.text: What the server runs and what the client carries. SSH from the segment is gated by the port-knock chain (exercise 5), so a plain connection is refused until a knock; vmctl reaches both over their NAT NIC regardless.

commands: timeout 3 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/172.20.2.1/22' || echo 'closed until a knock (exercise 5); vmctl reaches it over NAT'

exercises.title: Key-based authentication
exercises.text: Generate a key pair on the client and read its type. ed25519 is short and fast; a 4096-bit RSA key is the heavier classic.

commands: ssh-keygen -l -f ~/.ssh/lab_key.pub    # the fingerprint line names ED25519
rm -f ~/.ssh/lab_key ~/.ssh/lab_key.pub ~/.ssh/lab_rsa ~/.ssh/lab_rsa.pub    # leave the home as you found it

exercises.title: Hardening sshd_config
exercises.text: Tighten the server and reload it, then put the file back. Validate with sshd -t before every reload so a typo never leaves the server unable to start.

commands: sudo cp /etc/ssh/sshd_config.bak /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl reload ssh    # back to the start

exercises.title: fail2ban bans a noisy client
exercises.text: fail2ban watches the auth log and bans an address after a few failures. The ban is on the lab segment only (172.20.2.0/24): the NAT side is in ignoreip, so vmctl's SSH is never touched. Always unban at the end.

commands: sudo fail2ban-client status sshd    # the jail, its findtime/bantime and who is banned
for i in 1 2 3 4; do sshpass -p nope ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o PubkeyAuthentication=no lab@172.20.2.1 true 2>/dev/null; done    # four wrong passwords
sleep 3; sudo fail2ban-client status sshd | grep -A2 'Banned IP'    # 172.20.2.2 is now on the list
sudo fail2ban-client set sshd unbanip 172.20.2.2    # clear it, or the next exercise cannot connect

exercises.title: Port knocking
exercises.text: SSH from the segment starts closed (an iptables chain that DROPs); knockd opens it for a source only after the sequence 7000, 8000, 9000, and the reverse sequence closes it again. vmctl's SSH comes over NAT and never enters the chain.

commands: sudo iptables -S KNOCKD_SSH    # DROP by default; a knock inserts an ACCEPT above it
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=5 lab@172.20.2.1 'echo the knock worked'

exercises.title: What a scan sees
exercises.text: Look at the server from the client the way an outside scan would, and find the trace it leaves in the server's journal.

commands: nmap -sV -p 22 172.20.2.1    # the SSH banner and version
sudo journalctl -u ssh --no-pager -n 20    # the connection attempts from the client
